header:
Date: 2026-12-08
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Ortiz (Redwood SE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Jonah Li (Redwood Product Security), Sara Patel (Nebula Head of Security), Omar Rahman (Nebula Platform), Evelyn Park (Nebula CTO), Diego Marquez (Nebula Infra), Lina Hu (Nebula Compliance)
summary: Nebula Fintech ran a security review focused on encryption at rest/in transit, KMS options (managed vs BYOK), and HSM integration. Nebula requires BYOK with HSM-backed keys for production, audit logging with 7-year retention for certain datasets, and data residency in EU. Redwood team outlined hosted vs private deployment tradeoffs and proposed a private pilot using customer's VPC with envelope encryption. Action items agreed: share BYOK/HSM docs, SOC2/ISO certs, and plan pilot.
topics: Encryption at rest: AES-256, envelope encryption
KMS options: Redwood-managed KMS vs customer BYOK (AWS/GCP/HashiCorp)
HSM integration and FIPS/Sanctions/Key import/export constraints
Audit logs and retention (7 years for PII)
Pilot plan and benchmark for latency/cost
transcript:
00:00:03 Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll kick off in a minute.. uh quick intros from the redwood side, i'm maya chen, account exec
00:00:10 Liam Ortiz: hi all liam ortiz, solutions eng, i'll walk through the technical bits
00:00:14 Sara Patel: sara patel, head of security at nebula, happy to be here
00:00:17 Evelyn Park: evelyn park, cto
00:00:20 Omar Rahman: omar, platform team
00:00:24 Maya Chen: great, goal for today is to confirm encryption and key management requirements and see how BYOK/hsm fits with redwood's private option
00:00:35 Liam Ortiz: quick agenda — encryption at rest, in transit, keystore options, integration steps, audit logs and next steps
00:00:46 Diego Marquez: real quick — we have regulatory requirement to keep eudata in eu region and some keys must be hsm backed, fips140-2 type evidence
00:00:55 Lina Hu: and compliance needs 7 year audit log retention for transaction PII, so need to confirm redwood can ship logs 
00:01:04 Priya Kapoor: thanks, we'll cover logs and retention — we have configurable log exports to your SIEM or GCS/S3, with retention policy options
00:01:12 Sara Patel: important: Nebula requires BYOK; we can't have redwood-managed keys for production. we also need key rotation controls and split access for key admin
00:01:25 Liam Ortiz: understood. our platform supports customer-managed keys — we call it BYOK — and can integrate with cloud KMS (AWS KMS, Google KMS) or with vault-like systems. for extra assurance we support HSM-backed keys via import or external key reference depending on customer platform
00:01:42 Evelyn Park: can you outline the difference between envelope encryption here and you managing keys? we worry about performance impact
00:01:50 Liam Ortiz: sure. with envelope encryption, data is encrypted with a data key (DEK) and that DEK is encrypted with a key-encryption-key (KEK) stored in your KMS. so at serving time we decrypt the DEK (or use an HSM to unwrap) which is a small crypto op, then the DEK is used locally in memory for model inference; the per-token overhead is minimal. it's the round trip to KMS that can add latency if you don't cache the DEKs locally — we do local DEK caching with TTL and per-instance secure storage of the in-memory DEK.
00:02:22 Omar Rahman: how does that work with dedicated vs hosted? if we go hosted, we'd have to give you key access or you call our KMS — any network egress concerns?
00:02:31 Liam Ortiz: hosted: we can either support a cross-account role where our service calls your KMS endpoint in your cloud, or you can import a wrapped key. cross-account calls mean network hops but we can route within region. for latency-critical workloads we recommend private deployment in your VPC — redwood private keeps key calls inside your VPC and you control the KMS endpoint.
00:02:49 Sara Patel: we need HSM-backed keys, we want attestations. can you integrate with our HSM (Luna/HSM) or meet AWS CloudHSM?
00:02:57 Jonah Li: yes — we have two patterns: 1) external HSM where you keep keys in your HSM and redwood calls an API to unwrap/crypt operations (we prefer an EKM style with remote key ops), or 2) import wrapped keys into our runtime but only after you provide a verifiable wrap/attestation. for highest assurance, EKM with CloudHSM or Luna is common. we can also support CloudHSM in the same VPC for private deployments.
00:03:25 Diego Marquez: if redwood calls our HSM, does that mean your pods need network access to our key manager? any risk profile there?
00:03:33 Priya Kapoor: in a private deployment we run control plane separated; the dataplane sits in your VPC and never leaves. the key calls happen inside your network to your KMS/HSM. our team provides runbooks to configure security groups and mTLS to the KMS endpoint.
00:03:50 Lina Hu: about key rotation — we require ability to rotate KEK quarterly and have deterministic rewrap for older data; can redwood handle re-encryption?
00:03:59 Liam Ortiz: yes — we support rotation workflows. when KEK rotates you can rewrap DEKs; we surface tooling to do bulk rewrap or live rewrap depending on dataset size. we also can keep historical DEKs for rollback windows.
00:04:13 Evelyn Park: audit logs — we need tamper-evident logs and chain-of-custody for key usage, plus export to our SIEM for 7-year retention. what's the mechanism?
00:04:25 Jonah Li: we emit key usage events (unwrap, wrap, rotate) and can push to your cloud logging or to syslog/HTTP webhook; for tamper evidence you can enable log signing and ship logs to your S3/GCS with immutability policies. we also support rbac and mfa controls around key admin actions.
00:04:44 Sara Patel: any certifications we can rely on? fips, pci, soc2, iso?
00:04:50 Priya Kapoor: redwood has SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 — we'll share certs; for FIPS / HSM assertions we rely on the underlying HSM vendor. if you use CloudHSM or Luna, those provide FIPS attestations.
00:05:02 Omar Rahman: about network in-transit encryption — do you support mTLS between our services and the redwood runtime?
00:05:08 Liam Ortiz: yes, all in transit is TLS1.3 by default; for private deployments we can require mutual TLS using client certificates managed by your PKI.
00:05:17 Diego Marquez: does redwood store keys in plaintext on disk at any point?
00:05:21 Liam Ortiz: no. DEKs are stored encrypted at rest using the KEK; in memory they exist only in secure process memory and are zeroed on process shutdown. KEKs are never stored on our side for BYOK flows — we only store wrapped keys.
00:05:33 Sara Patel: curious about backups — if you snapshot the instance, could keys be leaked in backups?
00:05:39 Priya Kapoor: backups only contain wrapped keys. the unwrapped DEKs are not persisted to backup storage. for extra control you can disable automatic backups or use your own backup encryption keys.
00:05:49 Evelyn Park: latency numbers — any ballpark for KMS unwrap added latency? we need p95 budget under 150ms for inference tail latency
00:05:58 Liam Ortiz: unwrap is usually sub-50ms to KMS in same region; with caching that's amortized across requests. the local DEK cache reduces steady-state per-request addition to single-digit ms. worst-case cold unwrap could be 50-120ms depending on HSM provider RPCs — hence private placement reduces WAN variability.
00:06:18 Omar Rahman: regulatory: can you guarantee keys and logs remain in eu?
00:06:22 Jonah Li: yes. for private we deploy dataplane in your EU region, and KMS calls stay in eu endpoints. for hosted, we can pin region and route to EU KMS endpoints but you would need to ensure cross-border access policies are satisfied.
00:06:35 Sara Patel: can you do key escrow or split custody? we want multi-person approval for key rotation 
00:06:41 Liam Ortiz: we support integration with your key policies for split custody; we can require KMS-staged approvals or use your HSM's quorum features. on the application side we also provide RBAC that separates key admin from infra ops.
00:06:55 Lina Hu: any known limitations with HashiCorp Vault? we run vault and want to keep it internal with transit secrets engine
00:07:02 Priya Kapoor: Vault transit works fine — we integrate with Vault's transit API for unwrap/wrap. need network route and mTLS so our dataplane can call the transit endpoint. we have customers doing that in prod.
00:07:12 Diego Marquez: what's required from our side to test BYOK in a pilot?
00:07:16 Liam Ortiz: we'll need a KMS endpoint, service account or cross-account role, a test key or wrapped key file, and firewall rules for the dataplane. we'll provide a pilot checklist.
00:07:26 Sara Patel: we also need to ensure audit trail for who requested model outputs that used PII; can you correlate request IDs to key unwrap events?
00:07:33 Jonah Li: yes — we correlate request IDs with key operations in the logs. we can link trace IDs so you can trace a model response to the key unwrap. logs include timestamps, operation, principal, request id — we'll share a schema.
00:07:48 Omar Rahman: do you support hardware-backed attestation like sigstore or TPM for the runtime image?
00:07:55 Liam Ortiz: we support signed images and can integrate with your supply chain tooling — we also do reproducible builds and can provide SBOMs. for attestation we can work with your team to add TPM-based attestation or use cloud provider's instance attestation where available.
00:08:10 Evelyn Park: ok, one more: if we want HSM but also need lower-cost dev environment, can we have a hybrid setup? dev uses redwood-managed keys, prod BYOK?
00:08:18 Maya Chen: yes that's a common pattern. dev and staging use our managed keys for speed, prod uses BYOK/HSM. we'll document segregation and env guards so keys aren't accidentally used in non-prod.
00:08:30 Sara Patel: any gotchas with key import formats? we use PKCS#11 on our Luna HSM, what do you accept?
00:08:36 Liam Ortiz: we accept PKCS#8 wrapped key blobs and support PKCS#11 workflows via an import step. for Luna we typically wrap via an export token and import into the runtime per our import checklist. we'll provide format examples.
00:08:50 Diego Marquez: also, cost — extra KMS calls plus HSM ops add cost. can you provide estimate for 50k requests/day?
00:08:57 Priya Kapoor: we'll model cost in the follow-up, include KMS API call cost and any HSM hourly costs if using CloudHSM. we can also show savings with DEK caching and batching heuristics to reduce ops.
00:09:12 Lina Hu: last question: retention and deletion — if a user requests data deletion, how do you ensure DEKs and wrapped keys are scrubbed?
00:09:19 Jonah Li: we have documented deletion workflows — deleting the DEK and its wrapped copy makes ciphertext unrecoverable; we also purge associated logs from accessible stores per policy and provide attestation of deletion on request.
00:09:35 Maya Chen: ok thanks — we'll send docs and certs. can we recap next steps?
00:09:40 Sara Patel: yes please
00:09:42 Maya Chen: action items: maya to share BYOK + HSM guide, liam to create pilot checklist, jonah to share log schema and sample audit events, ev to confirm timeline — all due by mid-december. schedule pilot week of dec 20th if that works.
00:10:03 Evelyn Park: that works for us, we'll get internal sign-offs this week
00:10:08 Maya Chen: perfect, thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar and artifacts
00:10:12 [meeting end]
notes: References: BYOK integration guide (link to be sent), HSM whitepaper (attached post-call), SOC2/ISO certs (shared via secure link), pilot checklist (to be provided).
